body: New clipboard image reading functionality lacks test coverage. The `readClipboardImage()` function in `src/utils/clipboard.ts` should have unit tests covering: (1) macOS clipboard detection with PNG/TIFF/JPEG types, (2) Linux xclip and wl-paste clipboard reading, (3) error handling when no image is available, (4) timeout and command execution failures. Additionally, the image paste behavior in InputBox should be tested.

Documentation comment is outdated. Line 24 mentions "pngpaste or screencapture fallback" but the actual implementation only uses osascript to extract PNG data. The comment should be updated to accurately reflect the implementation.
```suggestion
 * macOS: uses osascript to check clipboard type and extract PNG data via a temporary file.
```

Temp file naming at line 54 uses `Date.now()` which could theoretically create collisions if multiple rapid clipboard reads occur simultaneously. Consider using a more unique identifier like `Math.random()` or UUID, or use Node.js's `mkdtemp` for safer temp file handling.

The Ctrl+V image clipboard handler at line 432 only checks for `evt.ctrl` but not `evt.meta`. On macOS, the paste key combination is Cmd+V, which may be reported as `evt.meta` depending on the terminal emulator. The handler should check for both `evt.ctrl && evt.name === "v"` (for Linux/Windows) and `evt.meta && evt.name === "v"` (for macOS), or it may not work on macOS terminals. Verify that the OpenTUI terminal emulator properly translates Cmd+V to Ctrl+V events across all supported terminals.

Merge into the existing `useKeyboard` hook

Two new `useKeyboard` calls (Ctrl+V + Backspace) before the existing one at line 497. Three keyboard listeners on the same component creates ordering issues.

The new Backspace handler fires before the existing fuzzy-mode backspace check (line 461). In fuzzy mode, backspace hits the new handler first, checks for `[image-N]` (no match), falls through. Works by accident, fragile.

Move both into the existing `useKeyboard`, before the `hasMatchesForNav` check.

Use `icon("image")` instead of hardcoded emoji

There is already an `image` icon in `src/core/icons.ts` with nerd font and ASCII variants. Every other indicator in the chat components uses `icon()`. Follow the same pattern.

Also: `UserMessageBubble` (line 624) has no image badge at all. Bubble-style users see no indication images were attached.

No model capability check

This sends `ImagePart` to whatever model is active. Text-only models (Haiku 3.5, DeepSeek, Ollama text models) will return API errors.

Either:
- Check capability and warn before sending
- Or strip images with a message: "Images removed, this model does not support multimodal input"

No multimodal metadata exists in the codebase yet, so a simple allowlist of vision models would work as a first pass.

8 second timeout is too long

Linux uses 3s. osascript clipboard reads are near-instant. On failure the `[loading…]` placeholder sits for 8 seconds.

```suggestion
      { timeout: 3000 },
```

Race condition: submit while `[loading...]` is in input

If the user presses Enter while the async clipboard read is still in progress, `finalInput` contains the literal text `[loading...]` which gets sent to the AI model as part of the message.

After submit, `resetInput()` clears the textarea. The `.then()` callback runs later, finds `tagIdx = -1` (textarea is empty), and silently does nothing. No crash, but the user sent garbage text to the model.

Fix: either block submit while `imageLoadingRef.current` is true, or strip `[loading...]` from `finalInput` before sending.

Bug: `isNvimAvailable` does not exist on `LspBackend`.

`LspBackend` uses `nvimBridge.isNvimAvailable()` internally but never exposes it as a class method. The optional chain returns `undefined`, `?? false` gives `false`. Nvim warmup is always skipped, even when nvim is running.

Fix: either add `isNvimAvailable()` to `LspBackend` that delegates to `nvimBridge.isNvimAvailable()`, or remove this check entirely. `warmupNvim` already guards itself (index.ts line 1009: `if (!nvimBridge.isNvimAvailable()) return false`).
Duplicate `var` in regex. It appears at position 5 (original) and again at the end after `val`. Remove the duplicate.
Move `LANGUAGE_ID_MAP` to module scope. This object is recreated on every `ensureDocumentOpen()` call. Make it a module-level `const`.
Missing `initError` field. The existing code passes `initError` to `updateBackend` for `lsp:nvim` (line 728). This no-probeFile path omits it. If the backend had an init error, it gets lost here.

`readdirSync` called once per extension marker per directory. For C# with markers `[".csproj", ".sln"]`, this reads the same directory twice while walking up the tree. Read entries once and check all extension markers against it.
1000 dirs with sync `readdirSync` could be slow on large monorepos. This runs during health check and warmup. Consider a lower cap or a time budget to bail early.

In the no-probe-file case, the comment says to mark both LSP paths as initialized so the UI doesn't hang, but `lsp:standalone` is set to `initialized: false`. Either set this to reflect the backend init state (e.g., `this.initialized.has(backend.name)`) or adjust the comment/semantics so the UI state is consistent.
```suggestion
            initialized: this.initialized.has(backend.name),
```

`nvimAvailable` is derived from `lsp.isNvimAvailable?.() ?? false`, but the LSP backend shown in this repo exposes Neovim availability via `nvimBridge.isNvimAvailable()` (and does not appear to implement an `isNvimAvailable()` method itself). As written, this will usually skip warmup even when Neovim is running. Consider either calling `nvimBridge.isNvimAvailable()` here (via a backend method) or adding/using an `isNvimAvailable()` method on the backend so the check is accurate.

The comment above this block says the BFS scan uses the same skip/depth as `findProbeFile`, but MAX_DEPTH/MAX_DIRS are now conditional on JVM detection and differ from `findProbeFile`’s limits. Update the comment to match the new behavior (or align the limits if they are intended to be identical).

`findProjectRootForLanguage` calls `readdirSync(dir)` once per extension-only marker (e.g. for C# it will read the same directory twice per level for `.csproj` and `.sln`). This is avoidable extra filesystem I/O on the hot path. Consider reading `entries` once per directory (or once per loop iteration) and checking all extension markers against that single listing.

`LANGUAGE_ID_MAP` is allocated on every `ensureDocumentOpen` call. Since this method can run frequently, consider hoisting the map to a module-level constant (or a `static readonly` field) to avoid repeated allocations and keep the function focused on document state.

910 lines is a lot for one file. Our copilot provider is 175 lines. This handles: CLI runner, app-server JSON-RPC client, prompt serialization, response parsing, language model adapter, login flow, browser opener.

Split into:
- `codex/client.ts` - app-server JSON-RPC (~150 lines)
- `codex/runner.ts` - CLI exec + prompt/response serialization (~300 lines)
- `codex/index.ts` - provider definition + login (~150 lines)

`doStream` calls `doGenerate` and wraps the result. Users see nothing until the full response completes, then everything appears at once. Every other provider streams incrementally.

You already parse `item.completed` and `turn.completed` line by line in `runCodexProcess`. Emitting deltas as they arrive should be straightforward. If real streaming isn't feasible, add a visible note in the provider description so users know what to expect.

`fallbackModels: []` and `contextWindows: []` means:
1. If app-server model list fails, users see zero models under Codex
2. Our token budget logic falls back to 128k default for all Codex models

Every other provider populates these. See `copilot.ts:127-168` for the pattern. At minimum add `gpt-5.2-codex` and `gpt-5.4` with their context windows.

Empty string here silently skips secret registration in `getProviderSecretEntries()` (filters on `!!(p.envVar && p.secretKey)`). Works but is an implicit contract. Add a short comment explaining why so future readers don't have to trace through the secret logic.

These `entry.id === "codex"` checks (3 total in this file) hardcode provider-specific behavior into a generic component. We already have one for copilot (line 109) and it was already tech debt.

Add optional fields to `ProviderDefinition` in `types.ts`:

```ts
noAuthLabel?: string;    // "login required" etc
authErrorLabel?: string; // "login/session error" etc
onRequestAuth?(): void;  // browser login, opens modal, etc
```

Then LlmSelector stays generic:
```ts
{provider.noAuthLabel ?? " · no key — Enter to add"}
```

Also lets us clean up the copilot "unofficial" badge with a `badge?: string` field.

This login logic is nearly identical to `startCodexLogin` in `LlmSelector.tsx` but diverges in small ways (icon, error color). Single source of truth: put the login-with-popup logic on the provider definition via `onRequestAuth`, then this command just calls `getProvider("codex")?.onRequestAuth?.()`.

Small behavior change from the old copilot hardcode: the old check had `entry.avail &&` so the badge only showed when the provider was authenticated. This version shows it always, so an unconfigured Copilot row would show both "no key" and "unofficial" on the same line.

Add `entry.avail &&` back:
```tsx
{entry.badge && entry.avail && !entry.loading && (
```

Otherwise looks good, rest is approved.

`descMaxWidth` doesn’t account for the two leading spaces rendered just before the description (`{"  "}`), so `displayDesc` can be 2 chars wider than the space that used to be available (previous logic effectively reserved space for the prefix + ellipsis). This can cause the description segment to overflow the row and rely on `truncate` in ways that change alignment. Consider subtracting those prefix spaces from `descMaxWidth` (or include the prefix in the string passed to the hook) so the returned string length matches the actual remaining width.
```suggestion
  const descMaxWidth = Math.max(0, innerW - cmdText.length - 12 - 2);
```

The command palette/autocomplete icon is derived via `icon(c.ic)`, but `openai` is not a defined key in `src/core/icons.ts` (NERD/ASCII sets). As a result these new Codex commands will render the literal string "openai" instead of an icon. Use an existing icon key (e.g. "model") or a Codex-specific glyph (consistent with the provider’s "⌘") so the UI shows an actual icon; consider updating the existing `/codex login` entry for consistency.

The PR description mentions adding a top-level `/codex` command, and `src/core/commands/codex.ts` registers it, but there is no corresponding `CommandDef` entry here. That means `/codex` won’t appear in the command palette/autocomplete list (unlike other “base” commands such as `/proxy` and `/lsp`). Add a `CommandDef` for `/codex` (likely as an alias to status) so it’s discoverable.

`icon("openai")` is not a defined icon key in `src/core/icons.ts`, so these Codex popups will render the literal string "openai" instead of an icon glyph. Use a real icon key (e.g. "model") or a Codex-specific glyph ("⌘") for the popup icon; apply consistently to the other Codex popups in this file as well.

`createOpenAICompatible()` is used elsewhere via `.chatModel(modelId)` (e.g. `providers/custom.ts`) rather than calling the returned object directly. If the provider object isn’t callable, `return provider(modelId)` will throw at runtime/compile-time. Use the chat-model accessor (or whichever accessor matches the intended endpoint) to construct the model.
```suggestion
    return provider.chatModel(modelId);
```

`contextWindows` ordering is reversed here: `SHARED_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` comes first, but context window matching is “first match wins” (`models.ts`). This causes generic patterns like `"claude"` from shared windows to match before provider-specific entries like `"claude-opus-4.6"`, returning an incorrect (too small) context window. Put provider-specific patterns before `...SHARED_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`.

`fetchModels()` for the new provider adds non-trivial parsing/HTTP behavior but there are no tests covering it. Other providers have mocked `fetchModels` tests (e.g. `tests/new-providers.test.ts`, `tests/custom-providers.test.ts`). Add a unit test that mocks `fetch` and asserts the returned `ProviderModelInfo[]` (and null on error/no key).

Same issue as `opencode-zen`: the code calls the result of `createOpenAICompatible()` as a function. In this codebase the OpenAI-compatible provider is constructed via `.chatModel(modelId)` (see `providers/custom.ts`), so this is likely incorrect and may break model creation. Switch to the appropriate accessor.
```suggestion
    return provider.chatModel(modelId);
```

The provider description says "GLM, Kimi, MiMo models" but `fallbackModels` also includes MiniMax models (`minimax-m2.7`, `minimax-m2.5`). Update the description to reflect the actual curated model set so users aren’t misled in the UI.
```suggestion
  description: "GLM, Kimi, MiMo, MiniMax models",
```

`fallbackModels` includes MiniMax models, but `contextWindows` doesn’t define any patterns for `minimax-m2.7` / `minimax-m2.5`. Because context window lookup falls back to substring patterns across *other* providers, this can yield inaccurate results (or no match) depending on naming. Add explicit context windows for these fallback models (the previous OpenCode provider had values for MiniMax M2.5).

This change removes the existing builtin provider id `opencode` and replaces it with `opencode-zen` / `opencode-go`. Several option maps are keyed by provider id (e.g. `src/core/llm/provider-options.ts` has entries for `opencode` in `PROVIDER_CONSTRAINTS` and `EPHEMERAL_CACHE`), so the new providers may lose gateway capabilities/caching unless those maps are updated (or `opencode` remains as a backwards-compatible alias). Please update the provider-id keyed logic accordingly.

`CustomReasoningConfig.effort` includes "none", but `buildReasoningBody()` currently *omits* the `reasoning` field when effort is "none". If callers set "none" expecting to explicitly disable reasoning/thinking on APIs that support it, this will silently fall back to the server default instead. Consider either forwarding `{ reasoning: { effort: "none" } }` when effort is "none", or remove "none" from the allowed union if omission is the intended behavior.

`createReasoningFetchWrapper()` returns a function typed as `(url: string, init: RequestInit) => ...` and then casts it to `typeof fetch`. `fetch` can be called with a `Request` object and/or with `init` omitted; if `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` ever calls the provided fetch that way, this wrapper will be incompatible. Prefer matching the real fetch signature `(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>` to avoid runtime edge cases and remove the unsafe cast.

The fetch wrapper mutates the `init` object in-place (`init.body = ...`). If the caller reuses the same `RequestInit` object across requests (or the SDK does internal retries), this can cause surprising side effects. Safer pattern is to create a shallow copy (and clone/replace just the `body`) before calling `fetch`.

New reasoning/thinking injection logic is introduced (`buildReasoningBody` + `createReasoningFetchWrapper`), but the existing custom provider tests don't assert that requests actually get the expected body params. Adding a test that mocks `globalThis.fetch` (or the SDK's fetch) and verifies the wrapper merges `effort`/`enable_thinking`/`thinking_budget`/`extraParams` into the outgoing JSON body would prevent regressions.
CodexCommandTheme - no other command module creates a custom theme interface. they all just call the theme store directly and use what they need.

icon("openai") - "openai" is not in the NERD or ASCII icon maps so icon() just returns the literal string "openai" as text. use providerIcon("codex") which resolves to the provider icon field. same issue in all the other popups in this file (logout, switch, login)

you register /codex as a handler here but there is no matching CommandDef in registry.ts for it. without that it will not show up in autocomplete/command palette. every other base command like /proxy has one
hardcoding the glyph instead of providerIcon("codex") breaks the abstraction. if the codex provider icon ever changes this will not update. the old code was correct here, revert this
why the dynamic import? checkProviders was a static import before and there is no circular dep issue. this adds complexity for no benefit, just keep the static import

unnecessary change. codex.ts already exists as a barrel that re-exports from ./codex/index.js. changing this to point directly at the subfolder bypasses that indirection for no reason. revert to keep the diff small on this high-traffic file

this hook runs per CommandRow so every visible row gets its own useMarqueeScroll instance. the inactive ones bail early and skip the interval which is good, but on every cursor move you are mounting/unmounting effects across all visible rows. not a real problem at our scale (maybe 20 rows visible) but if the palette ever gets bigger or we reuse this pattern elsewhere it could get chatty. worth keeping in mind

deps use .length  instead of text, if two different descriptions happen to have the same length the effect will not re-run and scroll position carries over from the previous one. unlikely in practice since active also changes on cursor move, but using  directly would be more correct and costs nothing
this is a nice self-contained state machine, would be easy to unit test the scroll/pause/reset cycle. not blocking but would be good to add a test file for it

skipping checkProviders() when cache exists means local providers that started after boot (Ollama, LM Studio) will show as unavailable until something else triggers a refresh. boot marks them unavailable, user starts Ollama, opens Ctrl+L, cache is non-null so checkProviders() is skipped, stale availability is shown.

instead of skipping it entirely, show cached data immediately (which you already do above) but still fire checkProviders() in the background so it updates when done. you get the instant open from cache and correctness from the async refresh:

Worth noting: scope precedence here (global wins) is the opposite of `src/core/skills/manager.ts:122-130,163` where project overrides global. Either flip the direction to match skills or drop a short comment on `INSTRUCTION_SOURCES` explaining why instructions invert the convention, so the next person does not have to go read both loaders to figure it out.

The precedence message ends up sandwiched between the project block and the global block in the final output. Reads as an orphan sentence the model can skip. If precedence is load-bearing, move it to the top as a framing preamble, or enforce it in the loader by dropping project entries whose `source` already has a global match.

Right now the claim is advisory only, and no test asserts which block wins when content conflicts.

Two gaps worth a follow-up:

1. No test exercises the `homedir()` default on L150 of `instructions.ts`. All three tests pass an explicit `homeDir`, so the prod code path is uncovered.
2. The 'both' test uses `toContain` only. Add an ordering assertion to lock in documented precedence:

```ts
expect(prompt.indexOf("global codex")).toBeGreaterThan(prompt.indexOf("project codex"));
```

A fourth test case where project and global define the same source with conflicting content would also be useful.

**src/hooks/useChat.ts:1175 uses compaction-request tokens as post-compaction context.**

Line 1175 (`compactUsage.inputTokens`) is the compaction model prompt size, not the next-turn context size. Adding Line 1179 estimate on top inflates `contextTokens`, so Line 1185 can remain artificially high and interfere with the reset path that depends on lower usage.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-        let estimatedTokens: number;
-        if (compactUsage && compactUsage.inputTokens > 0) {
-          // inputTokens already includes the full prompt, but we also need to account for
-          // the recent messages that weren't compacted. Add char-estimate for those.
-          const recentChars = newCoreChars;
-          const recentTokenEstimate = Math.ceil(recentChars / charsPerToken);
-          estimatedTokens = compactUsage.inputTokens + recentTokenEstimate;
-        } else {
-          estimatedTokens = Math.ceil(afterChars / charsPerToken);
-        }
+        // Post-compaction context should be estimated from post-compaction messages,
+        // not from the compaction model request usage.
+        const estimatedTokens = Math.ceil(afterChars / charsPerToken);
```
</details>

Line 1207 and Line 1208 fall back to `prev.cacheRead/cacheWrite` even though this block resets usage with `...ZERO_USAGE`. If compaction usage omits cache details, old cache totals leak into the new post-compaction baseline.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>


Yes. PowerShell’s New-ScheduledTaskAction -Argument parameter is a single String that Task Scheduler will treat as part of the command line (not a list of individually-parsed arguments) [1]. What that means for quoting/escaping: 1) You must build a command-line string yourself. If any individual argument (argument payload, paths, etc.) contains spaces, you must quote that part of the string so Task Scheduler/Windows parses it as one argument [2]. 2) If any part contains double quotes (") you must escape/encode them for the resulting “outer” command line that Task Scheduler receives. Practically, for nested quoting you typically use double quotes around the whole value passed as -Argument, then escape embedded " characters as \" (PowerShell) so that Task Scheduler ultimately sees the quotes correctly. A common working pattern from field reports is to use inner single quotes around arguments to avoid needing to escape many quotes (for example when creating tasks with schtasks /tr) [3]. Concrete examples A) Passing an argument that contains spaces (recommended: quote the argument portion) -Argument should contain something like: "<argument with spaces>" (the embedded quotes are part of the command line string) [2]. B) Passing an argument that itself contains quotes Use nested quoting so the embedded quotes survive as literal characters for the target program. One commonly working approach is: wrap the program/argument that needs quoting in single quotes inside the -Argument string (so you don’t have to escape inner double-quotes), e.g. a schtasks example uses /tr "'C:\Program Files (x86)\etc\test.exe' arg1 'arg 2 with spaces' arg3" [3]. Key point: PowerShell itself already parsed -Argument as a single string. Task Scheduler then parses that string as a command line. Therefore you must apply Windows/Task-Scheduler command-line quoting rules inside the -Argument value, rather than expecting PowerShell to split it into multiple arguments for you [1][2].
